absent: Filesystem specific implementations of metadata write, eviction, and metadata synchronization hooks and their error contracts.
Writeback queue ownership selection, thread scheduling, and full control lifecycle outside single inode processing.
Complete inode state flag enumeration and all transitions beyond the observed synchronization, dirty, freeing, cleared, isolation, pinning, and metadata flags.
Lock context creation and acquisition paths and normal release paths outside teardown leak reporting.
Dentry prune and release hook contracts and shrink list management outside the kill path.
Mount slow put path, namespace detachment, and expiry marking policy.
Page cache tag lifecycle and folio reclaim interaction beyond the tagged query.
Superblock operation table layout and notification backend delivery when enabled.

findings.text: Single inode writeback service processes one inode under a writeback control. It writes data pages from the associated mapping, optionally waits for data, propagates lazy timestamps, clears dirty state, conditionally writes metadata, optionally waits for metadata completion, and returns the first error observed.

Caller must already hold the inode under synchronization state when invoking single inode writeback. The implementation warns if that synchronization flag is absent at entry, treating it as a contract violation rather than acquiring it internally.

Full synchronous mode without external sync context waits for data pages after page writeback and folds any wait error into the result only if no earlier error occurred. Other modes skip this wait, leaving completion to the caller or an external path.

When the inode carries lazy timestamp dirtiness, the writeback path asks the filesystem to convert that lazy state into regular dirty state if operating in full synchronous mode or if the configured expiry interval after the recorded dirty time has passed.

Dirty state is sampled and cleared only after data write and timestamp handling, so redirty during those steps is not lost. Under the inode spinlock the current dirty bits are captured and cleared, a memory barrier orders visibility with concurrent dirtier, and page dirtiness is reinstated when the mapping still shows tagged pages.

If the mapping shows no tagged dirty pages but a network filesystem writeback pin remains without page dirtiness, the pin is cleared, an unpinned indicator is set in the control, and the captured dirty set is extended to force a metadata write for that transition.
Metadata write is skipped when the only captured dirtiness was page dirtiness. Otherwise the inode metadata writer is invoked and its error is preserved as the result when no earlier error occurred.

Full synchronous mode without external sync context additionally drains pending metadata output when a metadata writeback flag remains. The flag is cleared under lock before delegating to the superblock metadata synchronization operation, with error folding as before.

Metadata writer delegates to the superblock write operation only when that operation exists and the inode is not a bad inode. Tracing surrounds the delegation. When either condition fails the routine reports success without action.
Badness is determined solely by whether the inode operation pointer equals the global bad operations object. No other state is consulted.

Metadata only synchronization entry builds a control requesting zero data pages and selects full synchronous mode when the caller asks to wait, otherwise unsynchronized mode, then runs single inode writeback with that control.
Mapping dirtiness query reports whether the page cache index carries the requested mark. It is used to decide whether page dirtiness must be reinstated after clearing.

Eviction requires freeing state and an empty reclaim link at entry. It detaches from writeback and superblock lists, waits for reclaim isolation and in flight writeback, invokes filesystem eviction or final page truncation plus clearing, forgets any character device association, removes the hash, wakes new state waiters, asserts the final freeing plus cleared combination, then destroys the object.

Both reclaim isolation wait and writeback drain occur while holding the inode spinlock, with the lock released across sleeps inside the wait helpers and reacquired before continuing. No new writeback starts once freeing is set, so waiting only covers already running work.

Character device detachment clears the device list link, nulls the device pointer, and restores the mapping pointer to the embedded address space, so later page operations use the generic mapping again.
Character device detachment serializes device list and pointer updates with the global character device spinlock.
Writeback list detachment returns immediately when the writeback list link tests empty with a careful check, which tolerates a second call after eviction already unlinked the inode.

Writeback list detachment acquires the owning writeback list lock before the inode spinlock, clears the queued for sync flag, reinitializes the list link, accounts depopulation, then releases in reverse order.

Reclaim removal and superblock list removal are both no operation when the respective link is already empty. Otherwise they unlink and update global or per superblock accounting under the appropriate lock.

Destruction detaches writeback association, releases security state, emits delete notification, frees lock context, adjusts superblock removal count when link count is zero, releases cached access control lists, decrements the global inode count, then either runs filesystem destroy plus optional free through deferred release or queues generic deferred release.

If lock context teardown finds any remaining flock, POSIX, or lease entries, it logs device, inode number, and per lock owner, flags, type, and identifier details to aid diagnosis rather than silently dropping them.

Lock context lookup returns no context when the inode operation flags lack the context flag or when the configuration provides only a null returning variant. Otherwise it returns the stored context pointer with acquire ordering.

Reclaim isolation wait must be entered with the inode spinlock held. It sleeps uninterruptibly until the isolating flag clears, dropping the spinlock while scheduled out and rechecking under the lock after wakeup.

Clearing destroys the page cache index, requires freeing set without cleared, requires empty writeback list and zero pages, then assigns the combined freeing and cleared state without taking the inode lock because no concurrent state changes remain possible.
Verity cleanup runs only when verity support is enabled and the inode carries the verity flag, minimizing cost for ordinary inodes.

Combined clear plus set of inode state flags asserts that the inode spinlock is held by the caller, while the raw assign variant performs an ordered store without locking for use in contexts without concurrency.
Hash removal is skipped for already unhashed or fake hash links. Generic drop reports that the inode should be dropped when link count is zero or when the hash link is already unhashed.

Delete notification helpers forward to the backend delete hook, with the remove variant additionally emitting a self delete event before the delete hook. Directory inodes get an is directory modifier on the event mask.

Event emission and watcher checks return immediately without action when the superblock carries no notification state or when no watched objects exist at the requested priority, and the non configured backend reports success without delivery.
Dentry unhash entry checks for already unhashed state before removing from the hash and invalidating the sequence count, making repeated calls safe.
Hash removal computes the bucket from the name hash and serializes hash unlink with the bucket lock.

Dentry reclamation marks the reference dead, notifies prune observers, removes from reclaim list when present, unhashes, detaches or unlocks the inode link, updates global counts, runs release, reschedules, then unlists from the parent and either frees immediately or leaves freeing to shrink list handling before possibly propagating to the parent.

Parent lock is taken only for non root entries after the child work and rescheduling, with nested ordering for the child lock during unlink. Parent reference decrement decides whether reclamation stops or continues upward.

Dentry memory is released through deferred reclamation except when never visible to readers or when external name handling requires a distinct deferred path, preventing use after free by concurrent readers.
Reclaim list removal clears the list flag and decrements unused and negative counters as appropriate, warning if the underlying list removal reports the object was not on the list.

Tree detachment marks the entry killed, completes any tree shrink waiters, then either detaches secondary roots under the superblock roots lock or unlinks from the sibling chain while skipping cursor entries so walkers do not miss entries moved by concurrent cursor motion.

Kill locking prefers trying the inode lock without dropping the dentry lock. On contention it holds read side protection across the transition, drops the dentry lock, takes the inode lock first, then retakes the dentry lock and revalidates that the inode link did not change, retrying while an inode remains attached.

Reference count is rechecked both before attempting inode locking and after the ordered acquisition, and failure to acquire in order or a newly taken reference aborts the kill without freeing, leaving the caller to retry later.
Mount reference release clears a cached expiry mark with ordered store before delegating to the non expiring put path, and tolerates a null mount argument as a no operation.

When the mount is still attached to a namespace as observed under read side protection, the put takes only a fast decrement path with ordering against count readers and never blocks. Detached or null namespace mounts fall back to a slow path.

The inode object carries distinct list nodes for reclaim, superblock membership, and writeback queues, plus a hash node for lookup, a device link for character devices, and separate counters for link count and page residency used by eviction and clearing decisions.

The dentry object carries a hash node for lookup, a sibling node for parent child chains, a reclaim node, a parent pointer that is self referential for roots, an inode pointer, operation hooks, flag bits, a combined lock and reference, and a deferred head for safe freeing.

The writeback control carries a synchronization mode selector, a remaining page budget, an indicator for external sync context, and an output flag reporting network filesystem unpinning observed during the run.
Metadata only synchronization requests zero data pages, distinguishing pure metadata work from data writeback in the control budget.
Root status is defined as pointer equality between an entry and its own parent pointer.
Verity status is defined as presence of a dedicated flag bit in the inode flags word.
Access control pointers with the low bit set denote uncached values that must not be released as ordinary pointers, so teardown checks that encoding before releasing each list.
Hash removal and waiter wakeup rely on both sides taking the inode lock and aborting sleep when the inode is found unhashed, so no additional fence is needed between removal and wakeup.
